# Behavioral Economics and Decision Science — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers

This hub maps the territory of behavioral economics: how humans actually make decisions, value things, and behave in markets—as opposed to how economic theory assumes they behave. The 29 concept pages here build from foundational ideas about human vs. rational decision-making, through mechanisms of mental accounting and self-control, to applications in pricing, fairness, and financial markets. The core thesis across all pages: **humans are not Econs (rational optimizers), and this difference is systematic, predictable, and economically consequential**.

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Hughes Six-Minute X-Ray: Practitioner Decision-Style Taxonomy

*Chase Hughes — *Six-Minute X-Ray* (2020), Chapter 10. The Decision Map cross-referenced here because it functionally operationalizes findings from behavioral economics on heuristic-driven decision-making — Hughes' six pillars are essentially practitioner-vocabulary descriptions of dominant System 1 heuristics (status-quo bias, novelty-seeking, social-proof effects, endowment-and-investment biases, purpose-bound rationality, reactance and identity-distinctiveness). Where the academic literature has documented these heuristics across decades of research, Hughes provides a field-deployable framework for *exploiting* them. The Decision Map is what behavioral economics looks like when re-engineered as an operator's tool. Source: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hughes-six-minute-x-ray|Hughes — Six-Minute X-Ray (2020)]]. Tag: `[POPULAR SOURCE]`.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/decision-map-six-pillars|Decision Map: Six Pillars]] — six-pillar decision-filtering taxonomy (Deviance / Novelty / Social / Conformity / Investment / Necessity) with per-pillar filtering question; bleed-rule continuum (pillars adjacent in ordering blend; speakers share two adjacent); structurally analogous to VALS psychographic segmentation, Cialdini's six principles, and System 1 heuristic catalogs but calibrated for real-time conversational deployment rather than survey-based assessment | sources: 1

*Companion collision stub at [[LAB/Collisions/hughes-decision-map-vs-cialdini|Hughes' Decision Map vs. Cialdini's Six Principles]] explores the orthogonal-axes vs. redundant-vocabulary question — whether the Decision Map and Cialdini's framework operate on different conceptual axes (target's filter vs. operator's lever) or describe the same phenomenon in different vocabulary.*

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Foundations: How Decisions Actually Get Made
*Foundational pages — read these first if new to behavioral economics*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/homo-economicus-vs-homo-sapiens|Homo Economicus vs. Homo Sapiens]] — The core tension between economic theory's rational actor fiction and how humans actually decide. All other concepts in this hub explain the specific ways humans diverge from the Econ model.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/loss-aversion-asymmetric-valuation|Loss Aversion: Asymmetric Valuation]] — The foundational mechanism: losses hurt ~2x more than equivalent gains feel good. Appears in nearly every behavioral phenomenon in this hub. **Shotton application**: loss framing dominates consumer choice; KFC chicken messaging [POPULAR SOURCE]

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/reference-dependence-and-anchors|Reference Dependence and Anchors]] — All value is relative to a reference point, not absolute. This mechanism generates most of the behavioral anomalies in economics: what feels expensive depends entirely on what you're comparing to.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/present-bias-and-hyperbolic-discounting|Present Bias and Hyperbolic Discounting]] — Steep discount rate for immediate future (days), equal discount for distant futures (years). Generates procrastination, addiction, diet failures. **Shotton application**: Amazon Prime reframes future convenience costs as present psychological benefit [POPULAR SOURCE]

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Decision Mechanisms in Detail

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Mental Accounting and How People Organize Money
These pages explain how humans mentally categorize money and create artificial constraints:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mental-accounting-framework|Mental Accounting Framework]] — How people psychologically segregate money into categories (rent budget, discretionary, savings) with different rules and loss thresholds. Creates artificial cash poverty despite nominal wealth.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/transaction-utility-bargains-ripoffs|Transaction Utility: Bargains and Ripoffs]] — The pleasure/pain of the deal independent of the product. A "good deal" (paying less than reference price) creates satisfaction beyond the object itself. Explains bundling, price transparency effects, and why negotiated prices feel better than posted prices.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sunk-cost-fallacy-mechanisms|Sunk Cost Fallacy: Mechanisms and Entitlement]] — Why people continue bad investments and stay in bad situations. Not irrational; reflects legitimate psychological mechanisms (loss aversion, sunk costs as proxy for commitment). The difference between sunk cost fallacy and justified commitment.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mental-budgets-and-segregation|Mental Budgets and Segregation]] — Money treated as segregated into separate accounts creates artificial constraints. "Pay yourself first" works through segregation, not willpower. Explains why people can simultaneously have credit card debt and cash savings.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/house-money-effect-windfall-spending|House Money Effect: Windfall Spending]] — Windfall money (tax refunds, bonuses, inheritance) activates different spending rules than earned income. Feels "free" to spend; weaker loss aversion. Explains spending behavior paradox: people save regular income while spending windfalls of equal nominal value.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/nominal-illusion-wage-frames|Nominal Illusion: Wage Frames]] — Same real outcome (wage freeze during inflation = real loss) feels different depending on nominal frame. Wage cut rejected; wage freeze accepted. Determines what people perceive as fair even when real outcome is identical.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/reference-price-as-entitlement|Reference Price as Entitlement]] — Once a price is established, it becomes a psychological right. Increases feel like violations; decreases feel impossible. Explains price stickiness in markets, customer anger at "unfair" price increases, and why fairness matters more than supply-demand.

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Self-Control, Time, and Commitment
How humans struggle with commitment to future intentions and resolve it:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/planner-vs-doer-dual-selves|Planner vs. Doer: Dual Selves in Conflict]] — Two competing decision systems: cool Planner (wants to save, diet, exercise) and hot impulsive Doer (wants to spend, eat, relax now). Time-inconsistent preferences: wants to be disciplined about future, impatient about present.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/present-bias-and-hyperbolic-discounting|Present Bias and Hyperbolic Discounting]] — Steep discount rate for immediate future (days), equal discount for distant futures (years). Generates procrastination, addiction, diet failures. Distinction between sophisticated (knows they'll fail) and naive (thinks they'll succeed) discounters.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/self-control-and-commitment-devices|Self-Control and Commitment Devices]] — Self-control is not willpower; it's environmental design. Commitment devices (autopay, accountability, penalties, habit formation) bind Doer to Planner's intentions without relying on willpower. Removing choice is more effective than increasing willpower.

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Fairness Norms, Markets, and Pricing
How fairness constrains economic behavior more than theory predicts:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/fairness-norms-in-pricing|Fairness Norms in Pricing]] — Prices constrained by fairness norms more than supply-demand. Cost visibility, profit margins, and universal application determine whether customers perceive a price as fair. Firms don't maximize short-term profit if it violates fairness.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/price-gouging-and-emergency-pricing|Price Gouging and Emergency Pricing]] — Extreme fairness violation: exploiting desperation triggers moral outrage. Firms choosing fairness-optimal pricing ($3.50) over profit-optimal ($8) because fairness violations destroy reputation worth more than gained profit.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/preference-reversals-selling-vs-buying|Preference Reversals: Selling vs. Buying]] — Willing to buy at $12, demand $25+ to sell (identical item). Loss aversion + endowment effect create the asymmetry. Explains valuation gaps in real estate, wage negotiations, insurance markets.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/perceived-fairness-and-preference-reversals|Perceived Fairness and Preference Reversals]] — Frame (buying vs. selling) activates different fairness standards. Same price is fair in buying frame, unfair in selling frame. Fairness is not objective but frame-dependent, creating systematic negotiation gaps.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/firm-reputation-vs-short-term-profit|Firm Reputation vs. Short-Term Profit]] — Profitable firms don't maximize short-term price. Fairness violations destroy reputation worth more than gained profit. Long-term profit maximization requires fairness constraints. Explains why gas stations don't gouge despite ability to.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/market-entry-and-fair-dealing|Market Entry and Fair Dealing]] — New competitors face asymmetric fairness constraints: incumbents can violate fairness norms (reputation buffer); newcomers cannot. Creates reputation equilibrium lock that prevents entry even with cost advantages.

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Investment Behavior and Trading Anomalies
How behavioral patterns create predictable market anomalies:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/narrow-framing-daily-targets|Narrow Framing: Daily Targets and Risk Aversion]] — Evaluating decisions in isolation produces excessive risk aversion. Single coin flip feels risky; ten flips feel acceptable (identical EV). Explains excessive trading frequency, reluctance to take long-term risks, unrealistic daily return targets.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/myopic-loss-aversion-portfolio-checking|Myopic Loss Aversion: Portfolio Checking Frequency]] — Checking frequency determines behavior. Portfolio checked daily feels too risky; checked annually feels acceptable (identical risk, different perception). Explains equity premium puzzle: investors underweight stocks not because stocks are objectively too risky but because frequent evaluation makes them feel risky.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/overconfidence-in-markets|Overconfidence in Markets]] — Traders overestimate skill and predictability despite incentives for accuracy. Persists through: attribution bias (wins = skill, losses = luck), weak feedback, recency bias. Leads to excessive trading, concentrated bets, underestimation of risk.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/equity-premium-puzzle|Equity Premium Puzzle]] — Stocks return 6% more than bonds; theory predicts 0.35% gap. Gap explained by myopic loss aversion: checking frequency makes stock volatility feel excessive. Solution: change evaluation horizon to match investment horizon (reduce checking frequency).

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/stock-market-bubbles-and-overvaluation|Stock Market Bubbles and Overvaluation]] — Bubbles driven by: overconfidence, herd behavior, narrative capture, loss aversion creating momentum. Five-phase lifecycle: foundation → takeoff → euphoria → peak → collapse. Rational investors cannot reliably pop bubbles due to capital constraints and timing risk.

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Heuristics, Biases, and Market Efficiency
How specific judgment shortcuts create systematic errors:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/availability-heuristic-and-fear|Availability Heuristic and Fear]] — Risk perception based on vividness of examples, not statistics. Plane crashes feel riskier than driving (vivid vs. routine). Drives insurance purchasing, financial market overreactions to news, systematic risk misperception.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/anchoring-and-adjustment|Anchoring and Adjustment]] — First number offered disproportionately influences final estimate. Adjustment insufficient; final estimate biased toward anchor. Critical in negotiations: first offer determines outcome more than fundamentals. Making the first offer is strategically valuable far beyond its merits.

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/efficient-market-hypothesis-and-limits|Efficient Market Hypothesis and Its Limits]] — EMH assumes rational actors; evidence shows markets are semi-efficient. Anomalies persist: equity premium, bubbles, professional traders outperform, seasonal patterns. Markets incorporate information well long-term but have significant short-term psychological distortions.

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Shotton: Consumer Application Layer
*Added 2026-04-24: Shotton, Richard — Hacking the Human Mind (2023). Behavioral economics applied to brand strategy and consumer choice. All claims [POPULAR SOURCE]. Two high-density and additional MEDIUM/LOW pages apply behavioral economics principles to real-world brand positioning and pricing. These are applications of the theoretical principles above.*

- **Loss-Aversion in Brand Messaging**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/loss-aversion-asymmetric-valuation|Loss Aversion]] — KFC messaging shift (from "gain more chicken" to "never lose regular size") increased sales through loss framing; identical product, different reference point | status: applied | sources: 2 (Thaler + Shotton)

- **Present-Bias Reframing**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/present-bias-and-hyperbolic-discounting|Present Bias]] — Amazon Prime converts future cost into present psychological benefit (free shipping feels immediate even though used later); reframes time discounting in brand experience | status: applied | sources: 2 (Thaler + Shotton)

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Moral Psychology and Cognitive Foundations
How emotional, physical, and identity-based factors distort judgment and decision-making beyond standard BE mechanisms:

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/effective-altruism-identified-victim-effect|Effective Altruism and the Identified Victim Effect]] — why a single face triggers generosity that statistics cannot; scope insensitivity, observer effects on charitable giving, and the architectural flaw in human altruism; the mesolimbic dopamine system traffics in faces, not numbers | status: developing | sources: 1

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/sacred-values-and-conflict-negotiation|Sacred Values and Conflict Negotiation]] — values that exist outside the rational trade-off axis entirely; attempting to resolve sacred-value conflicts with material incentives backfires; why apologies and symbolic concessions matter more than money in intractable disputes | status: developing | sources: 1

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/embodied-cognition-and-moral-judgment|Embodied Cognition and Moral Judgment]] — physical sensations unconsciously alter moral and economic judgments; heavy clipboards make candidates seem more serious; rough textures make social interactions feel rougher; the brain cannot cleanly separate literal from metaphorical sensation | status: developing | sources: 1

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/tennis-time-vs-beach-time|Tennis Time vs. Beach Time]] — two neurochemically distinct cognitive modes triggered by perceived control; threat narrows attention and compresses decision space (Tennis Time); safety widens attention and enables creative integration (Beach Time); switches between them shape decision quality | status: stable | sources: 1

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/pride-epistemic-foundation|Pride as Epistemic Foundation]] — emotional investment in a group, leader, or ideology becomes the basis for what counts as evidence; pride functions as a cognitive shield that resolves dissonance by dismissing contradicting evidence rather than updating beliefs | status: developing | sources: 2

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Influence Mechanisms: Bias, Exposure, and Distinctiveness
*Cognitive and social effects that shape judgment and persuasion*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/endowment-effect-ownership-premium|Endowment Effect — Ownership Premium]] — perceived value inflates when ownership is established; loss aversion amplified | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/illusion-of-effort|Illusion of Effort]] — effort cues increase perceived value and quality of outcomes | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mere-exposure-effect|Mere Exposure Effect]] — repeated exposure increases liking independent of content or quality | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/pratfall-effect|Pratfall Effect]] — minor errors increase likeability in competent individuals; credibility mechanics | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/red-sneakers-effect|Red Sneakers Effect]] — deliberate norm violation signals high status and confident nonconformity | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/supposedly-irrelevant-factors|Supposedly Irrelevant Factors]] — contextual variables deemed irrelevant that systematically shift decisions | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/von-restorff-effect-distinctiveness|Von Restorff Effect — Distinctiveness]] — isolated distinctive items receive disproportionate attention and recall | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/stolen-thunder-technique|Stolen Thunder Technique]] — preemptive disclosure of damaging information reduces its impact when revealed by others | status: stable | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/messenger-effect-source-credibility|Messenger Effect — Source Credibility]] — message reception shaped by perceived credibility of the source, independent of content | status: stable | sources: 2


## Key Tensions in This Area

- **Rational vs. Adaptive**: Are behavioral phenomena "irrational" (violating logic) or "adaptive" (optimizing for real-world constraints)? SIFs, sunk costs, and fairness norms look irrational in theory but make sense when accounting for how humans evaluate tradeoffs.

- **Individual vs. Market Level**: Do individual behavioral anomalies aggregate to market-level irrationality? Some do (bubbles, herding). Others don't (fairness constraints reduce profit-maximization at individual level but increase long-term profit). The relationship is complex.

- **Frame Effects as Bug or Feature**: Are preference reversals and fairness reversals errors in judgment or legitimate ways humans handle uncertainty? Fairness creates negotiation friction but also stabilizes ownership and prevents constant retrading.

- **Behavior vs. Preference**: Do behavioral anomalies reveal true preferences (people actually prefer fairness) or violations of true preferences (people want to maximize but fail)? The answer differs by domain: fairness feels like true preference; present bias feels like violation.

## Cross-Domain Connections

**History**: [[ARCHIVES/concepts/history/machiavellian-realpolitik|Machiavellian Realpolitik]] — Rulers face fairness and reference-dependence constraints identical to those facing markets. New princes cannot violate fairness norms; established rulers have reputation capital. Political behavior mirrors market behavior through the same psychological mechanisms.

**Eastern Spirituality**: Behavioral economics mirrors contemplative traditions' analysis of how humans manufacture suffering through attachment to reference points, loss aversion, and narrow framing. The psychology of desire and equanimity in spiritual traditions is the obverse of behavioral economic mechanisms.


## Related Hubs

- None yet — this is the primary behavioral economics hub. If concepts around neuroeconomics, evolutionary psychology applied to economics, or behavioral finance grew to 10+ pages, would splinter into sub-hubs.

## Structural Notes

**Hub Status**: COMPLETE with Shotton applications layer — 29 core behavioral economics concept pages from Thaler's Misbehaving integrated and organized. Shotton (2023) application layer added 2026-04-24, showing how these principles manifest in brand strategy and consumer choice.

# Bioenergetics and Character Structure — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers
Fourteen pages from Lowen's *The Voice of the Body* covering the bioenergetic theory of character, repression, and vitality. Lowen's argument is that every chronic psychological defense has a corresponding chronic muscular tension — that the body is not a vessel for the mind but the other way around: character is what the body has agreed to. This hub maps that claim across its structural, diagnostic, and therapeutic dimensions. Single-source cluster — all 14 pages derive from Lowen (practitioner); priority scholarly additions flagged in Tensions.

## BEGINNER LEVEL — What Bioenergetics Is: The Body-Psychology Foundation
*Read these first — they establish the theoretical architecture.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/character-armor-and-muscular-tension|Character Armor and Muscular Tension]] — the foundational claim: Reich's character armor as literal muscular holding; how chronic psychological defense becomes chronic bodily contraction; armor as the body accepting the verdict of childhood
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/bioenergetic-pleasure-theory|Bioenergetic Pleasure Theory]] — pleasure as expansion, anxiety as contraction; the bioenergetic account of mental health as a bodily capacity, not a cognitive state; why understanding health requires understanding pleasure

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Character Structure: The Body as Frozen History
*How chronic tension patterns produce recognizable personality types.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/bodily-repression-mechanism|Bodily Repression Mechanism]] — how specific muscular contractions correspond to specific repressed contents; the geography of repression in the body; why talking about what the body is holding is less effective than releasing it
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/consciousness-pyramid-lowen|Consciousness Pyramid (Lowen)]] — Lowen's model of consciousness as a vertical axis from body to spirit; the argument that spiritual ascent that bypasses the body is dissociation, not transcendence
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/psychopathic-character-structure|Psychopathic Character Structure]] — the character built around denial of feeling and the will to dominate; the bodily signature; the difference between the classic psychopath and the phallic-narcissistic variant
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/horror-and-the-as-if-personality|Horror and the As-If Personality]] — the schizoid-adjacent structure that performs emotion without experiencing it; "as if" as description of the gap; the body's disconnection from the face
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/shock-illness-character|Shock, Illness, and Character]] — how acute shock and chronic illness both reshape character structure; the body's attempt to survive what it cannot process; character as wound architecture

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Vital Force and Energy
*The energetic substrate: what gets suppressed, how it returns, what its absence costs.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/will-to-live-and-wish-to-die|Will to Live and Wish to Die]] — the bioenergetic account of depression as a withdrawal of life energy, not a cognitive distortion; why the wish to die is not pathological but a response to a life that has become unbearable to the body
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/natural-aggression-and-violence|Natural Aggression and Violence]] — the distinction between natural aggression (life force moving outward) and violence (aggression without feeling, without contact); suppressed aggression as prerequisite for explosive violence
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/fear-of-pleasure|Fear of Pleasure]] — why pleasure is threatening: the charge that approaches pleasure also approaches the original wound; why people sabotage exactly what they claim to want
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/orgastic-potency|Orgastic Potency]] — Reich's concept, taken up by Lowen: full energetic discharge as the criterion of health; the argument that most people's chronic tension prevents full discharge and this is not a peripheral problem but the central one
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/beauty-grace-health-triad|Beauty, Grace, and Health Triad]] — Lowen's argument that beauty and grace are not aesthetic categories but signs of biological vitality; when the body is free, it moves gracefully; health is visible

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Synthesis: Where the Body Meets the Soul
*Integration of character, sexuality, and individuation.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/individuation-death-sex-personality|Individuation, Death, Sex, and Personality]] — the convergence of the three great biological forces (individuation/death/sex) as the engine of personality; the person who has not faced these has not yet become themselves
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/lowen-sex-personality-1962|Lowen — Love and Orgasm (1962)]] — Lowen's earlier synthesis: the relationship between love, sexuality, and psychological health before the full bioenergetic framework was named

---

---

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Cardiac Psychology and Heart-Body Integration

*Lowen's later clinical work focused on the heart as both a literal organ and the psychological center of the person — the locus of love, connection, and feeling. These pages extend the bioenergetic framework from character structure and sexuality into cardiac vulnerability, love deprivation, and the body's response to loss. The central clinical claim: heart disease is not primarily mechanical; it is relational and energetic.*

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Cardiac Mechanism Pages
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/love-deprivation-and-heart-closure|Love Deprivation and Heart Closure]] — the cardiac consequences of chronic emotional deprivation; how the heart contracts around the wound of unmet love; the body's literal response to relational absence | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/loss-of-vital-connections|Loss of Vital Connections]] — how severed relational ties deplete the bioenergetic system; the physiology of grief and disconnection; what the body does when its vital attachments are cut | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/rigidity-vs-collapse|Rigidity vs. Collapse]] — the two poles of bioenergetic failure: chronic muscular rigidity (holding against feeling) vs. collapse (the body giving up); how both produce cardiac vulnerability through different mechanisms | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/type-a-coronary-prone-personality|Type A: Coronary-Prone Personality]] — Lowen's bioenergetic reading of Type A behavior; the muscular and energetic architecture of the driven, hostile pattern; why chronic anger without discharge damages the heart | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/hostility-suppressed-anger-and-norepinephrine|Hostility, Suppressed Anger, and Norepinephrine]] — the biochemical mechanism: chronic suppressed hostility elevates norepinephrine; the connection from psychological pattern to coronary event | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/retirement-as-acute-cardiac-trigger|Retirement as Acute Cardiac Trigger]] — why retirement precipitates cardiac events; the sudden loss of purposive activity as bioenergetic depletion; the body collapses when the drive structure is removed | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sudden-cardiac-death-and-ventricular-fibrillation|Sudden Cardiac Death and Ventricular Fibrillation]] — the acute mechanism of cardiac death from a bioenergetic perspective; the role of emotional shock in ventricular fibrillation; sudden death as the body's final energetic discharge | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sunds-sleep-paralysis|SUNDS and Sleep Paralysis]] — Sudden Unexplained Nocturnal Death Syndrome as a bioenergetic phenomenon; the cardiac event during the vulnerability of sleep; cultural and physiological dimensions | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/asthma-as-heart-lung-connection|Asthma as Heart-Lung Connection]] — Lowen's reading of asthma as a cardiac-pulmonary expression of suppressed crying and grief; the respiratory restriction as character armor at the chest | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/symbiotic-fusion-and-mothers-emotional-state|Symbiotic Fusion and Mother's Emotional State]] — the earliest cardiac imprinting; how the mother's own energetic state (anxiety, depression, numbness) becomes the infant's baseline cardiac pattern | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/weaning-trauma-and-early-oral-deprivation|Weaning Trauma and Early Oral Deprivation]] — how premature weaning creates the foundational love-deprivation pattern; the oral-cardiac connection; the body's earliest experience of loss | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sex-without-love-vs-love-without-sex|Sex Without Love vs. Love Without Sex]] — the dissociation of eros and agape in the heart-body system; how each partial form creates specific cardiac vulnerabilities; what integration requires | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/frigidity-and-sexual-unresponsiveness|Frigidity and Sexual Unresponsiveness]] — the bioenergetic account of sexual unresponsiveness as character armor at the pelvis and heart; the relational and cardiac dimensions | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/impotence-and-erectile-dysfunction|Impotence and Erectile Dysfunction]] — the bioenergetic reading of erectile dysfunction as energy block, not mechanical failure; the cardiac-genital energetic circuit | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/full-orgasm-as-whole-body-integration|Full Orgasm as Whole-Body Integration]] — the orgasm as the criterion of bioenergetic health across the full body, not just the genitals; what full-body involvement requires and what prevents it | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/orgasm-as-proof-of-integration|Orgasm as Proof of Integration]] — the clinical use of orgastic capacity as a diagnostic marker; what the quality of energetic discharge reveals about character structure and health | status: developing | sources: 1

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Cardiac Clinical Case Studies
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-cardiac-crisis-as-wake-up-call|Case: Cardiac Crisis as Wake-Up Call]] — clinical case of a heart event precipitating the psychological work that had been avoided; the crisis as forced encounter with the body's truth | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-person-healed-through-breathing-and-grounding|Case: Healing Through Breathing and Grounding]] — clinical case demonstrating bioenergetic recovery through sustained work with breath and body grounding; the mechanism of healing | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-sudden-cardiac-death-after-loss|Case: Sudden Cardiac Death After Loss]] — clinical case illustrating the bioenergetic model of grief-precipitated cardiac death; the body's response to severed vital connection | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-the-daughter-searching-for-father-love|Case: The Daughter Searching for Father Love]] — clinical case of a woman whose cardiac and relational patterns were organized around the deprivation of paternal love; the heart as searcher | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-the-high-achieving-executive-with-silent-heart-damage|Case: The High-Achieving Executive with Silent Heart Damage]] — clinical case of Type A achievement masking progressive cardiac damage; the body paying the price the persona refuses to acknowledge | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-the-man-who-feared-his-own-success|Case: The Man Who Feared His Own Success]] — clinical case illustrating how success-fear organized both the psychological and the cardiac pattern; the bioenergetic sabotage mechanism | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-the-married-woman-without-sexual-pleasure|Case: The Married Woman Without Sexual Pleasure]] — clinical case of sex-love dissociation producing both relational and somatic dysfunction; the cardiac dimension of pleasureless sex | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/case-the-rigid-collapsed-couple-in-therapy|Case: The Rigid-Collapsed Couple in Therapy]] — clinical case of a couple where one partner carried rigidity and the other collapse; how complementary character structures create relational systems | status: developing | sources: 1


## Key Tensions

**Lowen's Catharsis vs. Levine's Titration**
The sharpest clinical disagreement across the somatic cluster. Lowen's bioenergetic therapy moves toward discharge — the direct expression and release of blocked energy through breathing, movement, and vocalization. Levine's Somatic Experiencing explicitly rejects catharsis as re-traumatizing: trauma is released through titration (small doses, pendulation, minimal activation). These are not minor stylistic differences; they represent incompatible theories of what the nervous system needs. Both frameworks agree the body is the site; they disagree on the mechanism. See: collision stub lowen-cathartic-vs-levine-titration.

**Pleasure as Health vs. Pleasure as Dangerous**
Lowen argues that the capacity for pleasure is the criterion of health. The fear-of-pleasure page documents that this is precisely what character structure suppresses. The tension: if the therapeutic goal is expanding the capacity for pleasure, and the presenting condition is fear of pleasure, the therapy itself may trigger the very armor it's trying to dissolve. This is not resolved in the Lowen corpus.

**Single-Source Status**
All 14 pages derive from one practitioner source. Priority scholarly additions: Reich *Character Analysis* (the original bioenergetic framework Lowen extends), van der Kolk *The Body Keeps the Score* (somatic convergence 40 years later), Porges *The Polyvagal Theory* (neurophysiological corroboration or challenge).

---

## Cross-Domain Connections
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/hubs/somatic-trauma-theory-hub|Somatic Trauma Theory Hub]] — Scaer's kindling theory and Levine's freeze-response both operate on the same bioenergetic substrate Lowen describes; the somatic trauma cluster provides the neurophysiological layer beneath Lowen's clinical observations
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/behavioral-mechanics/subject-profiling-and-btoe|Subject Profiling and BToE]] — Chase Hughes' behavioral profiling reads the same bodily signals (baseline, microexpressions, postural shifts) that Lowen argues are the readable surface of character structure; tactical reading vs. therapeutic understanding of the same body

# Ego Development Theory Hub — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers
Cook-Greuter's nine-stage Sentence Completion Test model of ego development — the most empirically grounded developmental psychology framework in the vault. Each stage is a qualitatively different structure of meaning-making, not merely a different set of beliefs. The cluster spans the complete arc: from pre-egoic undifferentiation through conventional identity construction, into post-conventional deconstruction, and finally through the transcendent stages where the lens turns on itself and dissolves. Primary source: Cook-Greuter 2013 (directly ingested, N=4,510 US adults). Secondary source: Leo Gura transcript trilogy (Parts 1–3, 2020) — practitioner-synthesizer; Layer B metaphysical additions tagged throughout.

**Population ground truth (Cook-Greuter 2013, Table 3):** Pre-conventional ~5% | Conventional ~75% | Post-Conventional ~15–20% | Construct-Aware ~1.5% | Unitive ~0.5%

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — The Stage Framework and Its Epistemological Core
*Read these first — they establish the framework's logic and the claim that matters: what separates stages is HOW you believe, not WHAT you believe.*

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Framework and Epistemological Core
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/ego-development-theory-framework|Ego Development Theory — Framework]] — full nine-stage arc; content vs. structure distinction; center of gravity; horizontal vs. vertical development; pre/trans fallacy; culture-as-Achiever-cap; construction-deconstruction arc; population percentages verified against primary paper | status: developing | sources: 4

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — The Stage Sequence

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Pre-Conventional Stage
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/pre-conventional-ego-stages|Pre-Conventional Ego Stages]] — Symbiotic (undifferentiated field), Impulsive (sensory-motor, crude good/bad), Opportunistic (zero-sum, magical thinking, shamelessness, no self-reflection); pre/trans fallacy warning; defense mechanisms table; why these stages appear across the adult population | status: developing | sources: 1

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Conventional Stage
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/conventional-ego-stages|Conventional Ego Stages]] — Conformist (group=reality, non-conformist conformity, shame engine, shadow floor); Expert (aboutism, last-word compulsion, 36.5% = largest single stage by SCT data); Achiever (culture-as-Achiever-cap, invisible materialism, begins noticing self-deception); defense mechanisms table; language diagnostic table; stage-specific depression types | status: developing | sources: 2

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Post-Conventional Stage
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/post-conventional-ego-stages|Post-Conventional Ego Stages]] — Pluralist (relativism as achievement, self-immunity illusion, logic as ego defense, epistemic vertigo, sub-personality emergence, performative contradiction, ~11%); Strategist (first stage that genuinely sees all lower stages, transformational mission, asymmetric legibility, self-inflation trap, blame-free relating, non-possessive love, ~5%); construction-deconstruction arc | status: developing | sources: 3

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Transcendent Stage
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/transcendent-ego-stages|Transcendent Ego Stages]] — Construct-Aware (web-weaving, language as technology, map/territory as felt predicament, grand theory trap, non-reified self, ego transcendence paradox, spiritual ego trap, self-deception jiu-jitsu, cross-paradigmatic thinking, existential aloneness depression, ~1.5%); Unitive (direct consciousness not belief, witnessing as primary, peaks become ground, controlled folly, dissolution of evil, self/other identity, mind vs. heart awakening, no depression type, ~0.5%); Layer A vs. Layer B distinction throughout | status: developing | sources: 2

---

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Spiritual Development and Applications

*Pages mapping consciousness expansion, spiritual maturity, and common pitfalls across the developmental arc*

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Spiritual Dimensions Across Stages
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/development-vs-spiritual-transcendence|Development vs. Spiritual Transcendence]] — The vertical development axis distinct from spiritual awakening; stages as meaning-making structures vs. direct experience; why Construct-Aware and Unitive stages do not require spiritual experience (possible but orthogonal) | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/spiritual-maturity-qualities|Spiritual Maturity Qualities]] — non-possessive love, non-judgmental compassion, tolerance for paradox, equanimity, non-reified awareness, detachment-with-engagement; stage-specific expressions (Conformist, Expert, Strategist maturity qualities differ); what marks genuine development vs. spiritual ego inflation | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/spiritual-emergency-concept|Spiritual Emergency Concept]] — when spiritual opening destabilizes the existing ego structure faster than it can integrate; differs from psychopathology; stage-dependent presentation (Conformist emergence as psychotic-seeming; Strategist emergence as existential crisis); integration requires stage-aware support | status: developing | sources: 1

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Spiritual Pitfalls and Bypass
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/spiritual-bypass-and-pitfalls|Spiritual Bypass and Pitfalls]] — using spiritual practice to avoid psychological work; stage-specific forms (Conformist: fundamentalism as certainty escape; Strategist: non-dual philosophy as avoidance of embodiment); why spiritual practice without psychological integration produces spiritual materialism | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/spiritual-thirst-and-misdirected-seeking|Spiritual Thirst and Misdirected Seeking]] — the genuine spiritual impulse mis-aimed at objects that cannot satisfy it; addiction-as-misdirected-seeking parallels; recognition of authentic desire underneath false targets | status: developing | sources: 1

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Consciousness Expansion and Experiences
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/meditation-consciousness-expansion|Meditation and Consciousness Expansion]] — state experiences vs. trait development; why meditation can open states without developing stage; advanced meditators at any stage; the critical distinction between temporary glimpses and structural development | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/unitive-consciousness-bliss|Unitive Consciousness and Bliss]] — direct experience of non-dual consciousness; the phenomenology of the unitive state; persistence of unitive states across daily life; relationship to ego stage development (possible at Strategist, characteristic at Construct-Aware/Unitive) | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/fruits-of-spiritual-maturity|Fruits of Spiritual Maturity]] — the practical outcomes and qualities that mark genuine development: increased capacity for presence, reduced reactivity, compassion as default, equanimity without dissociation, embodied non-attachment | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/full-human-consciousness-model|Full Human Consciousness Model]] — integration of all consciousness dimensions (embodied presence, intellectual clarity, emotional maturity, spiritual openness); the argument that high-stage development requires activation across all dimensions, not just cognitive structure or spiritual experience | status: developing | sources: 1

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Mystical Experience Interface
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mystical-experience-stage-interpretation|Mystical Experience Stage Interpretation]] *(cross-domain)* — stage as interpretive container for genuine mystical experience; same phenomenological experience pours into radically different containers by stage; Conformist (exclusive truth claim), Expert/Achiever (neurological domestication), Pluralist (egalitarian mysticism), Strategist (developmental vision), Construct-Aware (spiritual ego usurps the glimpse), Unitive (container dissolves into content) | status: developing | sources: 3

## ADVANCED LEVEL — Ego Development Applied to Psychology and Spirituality
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/spirituality-vs-consciousness|Spirituality vs. Consciousness]] — spirituality as values/meaning system; consciousness as capacity for awareness; the distinction that allows genuine development work to be orthogonal to spiritual traditions | status: developing | sources: 1

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Clinical and Existential Applications

*Ego development concepts applied to clinical practice, existential encounters, and therapeutic dynamics. These pages extend the developmental framework into the consulting room and into the terrain of mortality, alienation, and the therapist's own psychology.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/alienation-the-necessary-separation-and-its-terrors|Alienation: The Necessary Separation and Its Terrors]] — the developmental cost of individuation; how the movement toward selfhood requires separation from embeddedness; why alienation is not pathological but the price of development | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/competence-progression-initiation-framework|Competence Progression: Initiation Framework]] — how genuine competence develops through initiation-like phases; the distinction between performed competence and integrated mastery; the framework for tracking developmental progression | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/conscious-vs-opportunistic-survival|Conscious vs. Opportunistic Survival]] — the developmental distinction between survival strategies that preserve consciousness vs. those that sacrifice it; how the choice between them tracks ego development stage | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/controlled-folly|Controlled Folly]] — Castaneda's concept: acting fully while knowing the ultimate groundlessness of all action; the post-conventional capacity to engage wholeheartedly with what cannot be finally justified | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/counter-transference-and-the-therapists-actual-feelings|Counter-Transference and the Therapist's Actual Feelings]] — how the therapist's ego development stage shapes what appears as counter-transference; the developmental dimension of the therapist's subjective experience | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/death-preparation-fear-management|Death Preparation and Fear Management]] — how different ego development stages relate differently to mortality; what genuine death preparation requires at the post-conventional and transcendent levels | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/negative-therapeutic-reaction-as-loyalty|Negative Therapeutic Reaction as Loyalty]] — the paradox where improvement produces symptomatic worsening; reframed as loyalty to the developmental system that produced the wound; the developmental interpretation of therapeutic resistance | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/psychological-magnification-through-imagery-and-language|Psychological Magnification Through Imagery and Language]] — how symbolic and linguistic frames amplify psychological states; the role of developmental stage in determining which frames are available; imagery as developmental leverage | status: developing | sources: 1


## Key Tensions in This Area

**1. Layer A vs. Layer B throughout the transcendent stages**
Cook-Greuter's phenomenological descriptions of Construct-Aware and Unitive (Layer A — verifiable against primary paper) vs. Leo Gura's non-dual metaphysical claims (Layer B — "you are God," "reality is imaginary," "all fear is illusion" — not Cook-Greuter's). Both layers are documented; neither should be cited as the other. See [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/transcendent-ego-stages|Transcendent Ego Stages]] Evidence/Tensions section.

**2. Stage self-diagnosis reliability**
The Strategist's self-inflation trap applies to all self-reported stage assessments. Leo Gura self-identifies as primarily Construct-Aware; his Unitive descriptions are partly aspirational. Cook-Greuter's SCT methodology (sentence completion, scored by trained raters) is the only externally validated assessment tool. First-person testimony is always suspect above the Achiever stage, where the developmental vocabulary for self-deception becomes increasingly sophisticated.

**3. EDT vs. Spiral Dynamics at high stages**
Cook-Greuter's EDT preferred over Beck/Cowan's Spiral Dynamics for Construct-Aware and Unitive descriptions: more personally scaled, more nuanced phenomenology, more precise about failure modes. Spiral Dynamics handles collective/social developmental dynamics better. Not competing models — different resolution at different scales.

**4. Ego transcendence paradox at Construct-Aware**
Trying harder to dissolve the ego reinforces it (the desire to transcend is itself the ego). Detachment becomes a new attachment. This is not solvable from within the paradox's frame. The contemplative traditions (Zen, Advaita, Trika) each claim working approaches; the vault does not yet hold their primary accounts. Open question: see [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/transcendent-ego-stages|Transcendent Ego Stages]] Open Questions section.

**5. Pre/trans fallacy — applies in both directions**
Mistaking pre-egoic regression for trans-egoic transcendence (the spiritually bypassing person who calls dissolution "awakening"). Also: mistaking trans-egoic development for pre-egoic regression ("they've lost their grip on reality"). Reliable behavioral diagnostic distinguishing these two does not exist in the vault. See [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/ego-development-theory-framework|Framework]] Live Edge.

## Cross-Domain Connections

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/shadow-integration|Shadow Integration]] — shadow formation is Conformist-stage architecture (group=identity → sealed room); sub-personality surfacing is Pluralist-stage developmental pressure; Strategist's integration is shadow work arrived at developmentally rather than therapeutically; Construct-Aware deconstruction and shadow work are the same project at different altitudes
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/grandiosity|Grandiosity]] — every stage produces its characteristic grandiosity using that stage's best tools: Expert uses intellectual competence, Strategist uses developmental self-knowledge, Construct-Aware uses self-transparency itself; the recursive diagnostic never bottoms out
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mass-movement-mechanics|Mass Movement Mechanics]] — Hoffer's frustrated self is the developmental psychology diagnosis of where evil comes from; mass movement is what happens when ego-bound survival minds escape themselves collectively rather than dissolving developmentally
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/eastern-spirituality/guru-tattva-and-dika|Guru-Tattva and Initiation]] — the guru tradition is selecting for Unitive-stage stabilization as its transmission prerequisite; EDT and Trika Shaivism are different vehicles arriving at the same destination
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/jinshin-doshin-dual-mind|Jinshin/Doshin — The Dual Mind]] — doshin (heaven-aligned, detached from motive) looks like Unitive-stage functioning from outside; EDT raises the question of whether doshin is stage-invariant or whether a Conformist practitioner's doshin and a Construct-Aware practitioner's doshin are the same state in different containers (collision stub filed: LAB/Collisions/edt-construct-aware-vs-doshin-practice-assumption.md)

# Evolutionary Psychology — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers

How evolution shaped human psychology across mating, morality, status, kinship, empathy, and motivation. Covers the selection pressures that produced human sexual strategies, moral sentiments, conscience, guilt, shame, jealousy, status anxiety, kinship recognition systems, the neurobiology of empathy and compassion, the dopamine system of pursuit, and the mechanisms by which we deceive ourselves. Core sources: Wright's *The Moral Animal* + Sapolsky's *Behave* (neurobiological substrate of evolutionary mechanisms) + Buss's *Evolutionary Psychology: The New Science of the Mind* (4th ed., 2014) — the canonical textbook providing the formal architecture (EPMs, EEA, Tinbergen's four whys, Levels of Analysis, Error Management Theory), survival adaptations (hunting, spatial cognition, disgust, pregnancy sickness), and the mating-psychology core (reproductive value, WHR, concealed ovulation, sperm competition).

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Foundations of Evolutionary Psychology

*The formal architecture — what an EPM is, where it was tuned, how to test claims about it (Buss EP4, 2014, Ch 1–2)*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/evolved-psychological-mechanism-six-properties|Evolved Psychological Mechanism: Six Properties]] — the unit of analysis in EP; six properties define it; key/lock metaphor; carpenter's toolbox vs. Swiss army knife; learning as specialized EPM | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/environment-of-evolutionary-adaptedness-eea|Environment of Evolutionary Adaptedness (EEA)]] — Tooby & Cosmides 1992 statistical-composite definition; not a place or time but a set of selection pressures; each adaptation has its own EEA; 99% hunter-gatherer claim | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/three-products-of-evolution-adaptations-byproducts-noise|Three Products of Evolution: Adaptations, By-Products, Noise]] — Tooby & Cosmides 1990 framework; umbilical cord/belly button/belly button shape; Williams's 4 criteria (efficiency, economy, precision, reliability) for identifying adaptations | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/tinbergens-four-whys-proximate-and-ultimate-causation|Tinbergen's Four Whys: Proximate and Ultimate Causation]] — Tinbergen 1951 four levels of explanation (immediate, developmental, function, phylogeny); Lorenz duckling example; foundational for distinguishing how vs why questions | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/domain-specific-vs-domain-general-cognitive-mechanisms|Domain-Specific vs. Domain-General Cognitive Mechanisms]] — central debate in EP cognitive architecture; Tooby/Cosmides Swiss-army-knife position vs. Chiappe/MacDonald domain-general extensions; Pinker's combinatorial-explosion argument | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/evolutionary-mismatch-stone-age-brain-modern-environment|Evolutionary Mismatch: Stone-Age Brain in Modern Environment]] — time lags between EEA and modern environment; "Stone Age brain in a modern environment" (Buss); fat preferences / snake fear / mate-value contrast effects | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/levels-of-evolutionary-analysis-and-hypothesis-generation|Levels of Evolutionary Analysis and Hypothesis Generation]] — General Theory → Middle-Level Theories (Trivers PI, kin selection) → Specific Hypotheses → Predictions; top-down vs. bottom-up (Singh's WHR as bottom-up exemplar); 8 methods + 6 data sources | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/error-management-theory-adaptive-biases|Error Management Theory: Adaptive Biases]] — Buss & Haselton 2000 formal theory; smoke-detector logic of asymmetric error costs; Descent Illusion, auditory looming bias, sexual overperception bias, commitment skepticism bias as paired EMT applications | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Survival Adaptations

*Combating the hostile forces of nature — Buss EP4 Ch 3*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/hunting-hypothesis-and-show-off-hypothesis|Hunting Hypothesis and Show-Off Hypothesis]] — Tooby & DeVore 1987 Provisioning vs. Hawkes 1991 Show-Off; meat as concentrated nutrition vs. costly-signaling display; cross-cultural meat-share data; ancestral subsistence economies | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/hunter-gatherer-spatial-cognition-sex-differences|Hunter-Gatherer Spatial Cognition: Sex Differences]] — Silverman & Eals 1992; Silverman/Choi/Peters 2007 40-country mental-rotation study; New 2007 ecologically valid plant arrays; small-effect caveat (Voyer 2007) | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/disgust-as-disease-avoidance-emotion|Disgust as Disease-Avoidance Emotion]] — Curtis/Aunger/Rabie 2004; Oaten/Stevenson/Case 2009; universal elicitors (rotting flesh, feces, parasites); Stevenson 2009 high-disgust-sensitivity → fewer infections; Tybur 2009 sexual disgust | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/pregnancy-sickness-as-embryo-protection-adaptation|Pregnancy Sickness as Embryo Protection]] — Profet 1992 hypothesis; Tierson 1985 food-aversion data; Yerushalmy/Milkovich 1965 N=3,853 (10.4% vs. 3.8% miscarriage rate); cleanest adaptationist case study | status: developing | sources: 1

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Core Foundations

*Principles underlying all downstream concepts*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/parental-investment-theory|Parental Investment Theory]] — differential investment by sex produces different mating strategies; female constraint = male competition; reproductive asymmetry drives psychological architecture; Buss EP4 enrichment: Trivers as middle-level theory + sex-role-reversed species (pipefish, Mormon cricket, poison-arrow frog) | status: stable | sources: 4
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/kin-selection-inclusive-fitness|Kin Selection and Inclusive Fitness]] — genes survive through relatives as well as offspring; explains nepotism, sacrifice for kin, altruism asymmetries | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/kin-selection-and-recognition|Kin Selection and Recognition: Evolutionary Logic of Genetic Relatedness]] — Hamilton's algebra (50% siblings, 25% cousins) + recognition systems across species; humans as cognitive kin-recognizers; green-beard effect showing how arbitrary markers hijack the kinship circuit | status: stable | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/reciprocal-altruism|Reciprocal Altruism]] — cooperation between non-relatives through reputation tracking; cheater-detection psychology as evolved auditor | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sexual-selection-in-humans|Sexual Selection in Humans]] — mate choice as selection force equal to survival pressure; costly signaling through display; intrasexual competition and intersexual choice producing human psychology; Buss EP4 enrichment: Darwin's two theories formalized + variance-asymmetry account of sex differences in risk-taking | status: stable | sources: 5
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/imprinted-genes-and-parent-offspring-conflict|Imprinted Genes and Parent-Offspring Conflict]] — genomic imprinting; mother- vs. father-imprinted genes pulling in opposite directions; the genetic civil war inside the developing fetus | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/primate-parallels-ancestral-behavioral-architecture|Primate Parallels: Ancestral Behavioral Architecture]] — bonobos vs. chimps vs. baboons vs. macaques vs. humans; aggression and cooperation patterns across species; ecological shaping of social structure; bonobo as existence-proof of alternative organization | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Mating Psychology and Pair-Bonding

*How evolution shaped human sexual strategy, attraction, jealousy, and commitment*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/reproductive-value-vs-fertility-distinction|Reproductive Value vs. Fertility Distinction]] — RV = expected future reproduction; fertility = current reproductive performance; long-term mating preferences track RV (younger), short-term mating tracks fertility (peak-age) | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/waist-to-hip-ratio-fertility-cue|Waist-to-Hip Ratio: Fertility Cue]] — Singh 1993 0.70 cross-cultural preference; Karremans 2010 blind-from-birth tactile preference; estradiol biochemical correlate; Sugiyama 2004a relative-position refinement | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/concealed-ovulation-and-paternity-uncertainty-adaptations|Concealed Ovulation and Paternity Uncertainty]] — ten lines of evidence for partial detection; lap-dancer tip data (Miller/Tybur/Jordan 2007); marriage as institutional solution; chastity + fidelity preferences as paternity-security mechanisms | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/sperm-competition-theory-and-physiology|Sperm Competition: Testes Size and Physiology]] — testes-to-body-weight ratio across primates (gorilla 0.018% / human 0.079% / chimp 0.269%); Wrangham 1993 partner-per-birth (human 1.1); Baker & Bellis 1995 sperm-count modulation | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/male-sexual-jealousy|Male Sexual Jealousy]] — paternity uncertainty driving monitoring and mate-guarding; escalates under divorce risk; Buss EP4 enrichment: 1992 forced-choice study (83% women > emotional vs. 60% men > sexual) + 35-replication record + Takahashi 2006 fMRI (men amygdala/hypothalamus, women posterior superior sulcus) + Strategic Interference Theory frame | status: stable | sources: 4
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mating-psychology-selectivity|Mating Psychology and Selectivity]] — female choosiness for indicators of resources and commitment; male preference for fertility/health cues; strategic inconsistency in both sexes; Buss EP4 enrichment: Adaptive Problems Table (6 problems → preference clusters) + 37-cultures study (N=10,047) + cross-decade replication 1939-1985 + Bakweri/successful-women falsification of Structural Powerlessness Hypothesis | status: stable | sources: 3
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/romantic-love|Romantic Love]] — evolved commitment device; produces pair-bond maintenance, sexual jealousy suppression of alternatives, parental investment binding; Buss EP4 enrichment: Jankowiak/Fischer 168-cultures evidence (88.5% prevalence) + acts-of-love research + Fisher/Aron/Brown 2005 fMRI caudate+VTA dopamine activation (cocaine-analog rush) + Schmitt 48-nation lower love in ecological-stress cultures | status: stable | sources: 3
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/parent-offspring-conflict|Parent-Offspring Conflict]] — offspring demanding more investment than parents want to give; sibling conflict; weaning wars; negotiation at biological/psychological interface | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/westermarck-effect-proximity-and-sexual-deactivation|The Westermarck Effect: Proximity and Sexual Deactivation]] — childhood co-residence ages 2-6 programs lifelong sexual aversion regardless of genetic relationship; kibbutz and Taiwan minor-marriage evidence; the kin-detector also generates contempt and moral disgust; Buss EP4 enrichment: paradigmatic specialized-learning mechanism + Lieberman/Tooby/Cosmides 2003 dose-response confirmation + Burkett/Cosmides 2006 deal-breaker rating | status: stable | sources: 2 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/oxytocin-vasopressin-bonding-dark-side|Oxytocin & Vasopressin: The Bonding Hormones and Their Tribal Shadow]] — bonding hormones with parochial side; in-group favoritism + out-group suspicion; de Dreu studies; pair-bonding mechanisms in prairie voles vs. humans | status: stable | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/oxytocin-vasopressin-temporal-discounting|Oxytocin, Vasopressin, and Temporal Discounting]] — bonding hormones in delay tolerance; how attachment shapes future-orientation | status: developing | sources: 1

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Morality, Conscience, and Guilt

*How evolution produced moral sentiments, conscience, guilt, and reputation-guarding*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/moral-sentiments|Moral Sentiments]] — guilt, shame, anger, gratitude as evolved emotional enforcement mechanisms for cooperation and norm-following | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/conscience-development|Conscience Development]] — guilt as learned punishment response; shame as reputation-guard; both operate without conscious intention (automatic moral policing) | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/guilt-gratitude|Guilt and Gratitude]] — guilt suppresses free-riding and maintains reciprocal alliances; gratitude binds cooperators; both neurochemically distinct from shame (internal vs. social focus) | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/shame-reputation|Shame and Reputation]] — shame as reputation-damage-avoidance mechanism; monitor/signal about social standing; drives concealment or status-recovery behavior | status: developing | sources: 2
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/cheater-detection|Cheater Detection]] — cognitive specialization for detecting reciprocal altruism violations; "if you take a benefit, you must pay a cost" logic; universal across cultures with variations in content | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/moral-judgment-neurobiology-pfc-insula-amygdala|Moral Judgment Neurobiology: PFC + Insula + Amygdala]] — three competing moral systems; deontological (vmPFC/amygdala/insula) vs. utilitarian (dlPFC); brain damage cases shifting moral judgment | status: developing | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/trolley-problem-in-the-brain|The Trolley Problem in the Brain]] — same arithmetic, opposite moral judgments depending on neural circuit engaged; Greene's neuroethics; 30/30/40 distribution of consistent deontologists, consistent utilitarians, context-dependent; parametric vs. strategic consequentialism | status: stable | sources: 1 | density: HIGH

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Status, Dominance, and Social Hierarchy

*How evolution structured human status-seeking and hierarchy psychology*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/status-hierarchies|Status Hierarchies]] — humans form ranked social orders; status affects reproduction and resource access; status anxiety drives behavior independent of conscious belief in hierarchies | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/serotonin-social-dominance|Serotonin and Social Dominance]] — serotonin availability correlates with social rank and confidence; low serotonin produces status anxiety and submission; evolutionary mechanism linking neurochemistry to social position | status: developing | sources: 1

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Self-Deception and Psychological Defense

*How evolution shaped the capacity and tendency to deceive ourselves*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/self-deception|Self-Deception]] — evolved capacity to misrepresent reality to self and others; allows appearing confident while managing risk; produces genuine (not strategic) belief; underlying mechanisms: attention control, narrative rewriting, selective memory; Buss EP4 enrichment: mate-value misperception under modern-environment contrast effects (Kenrick et al. 1989/1994; Mishra/Clark/Daly 2007); environmental-mismatch route to self-deception | status: stable | sources: 5

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Empathy, Compassion, and Social Cognition

*The neurobiology of feeling-for and feeling-with — and why they aren't the same*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/empathy-neurobiology-acc-insula-emotional-contagion|Empathy Neurobiology: ACC, Insula, and Emotional Contagion]] — pain-matrix activation when observing others' suffering; insula's role in disgust and empathic resonance; ACC as the suffering-recognition system; why empathy can paralyze rather than enable action | status: stable | sources: 1 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/compassion-versus-empathy-buddhist-contemplative-practice|Compassion vs. Empathy: When Detachment Heals Better Than Feeling]] — Sapolsky + Jamison + Buddhist sources on the empathy/compassion split; Ricard's neuroimaging; mesolimbic dopamine activation in compassion vs. amygdala in empathy; detachment as prerequisite for prosocial action | status: stable | sources: 3 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mirror-neurons-empathy-social-understanding|Mirror Neurons & Empathy: Social Understanding Systems]] — Rizzolatti/Gallese discovery; cross-modal activation; the two-systems empathy account; Hickok's "myth of mirror neurons" critique preserved as tension | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/mirror-neurons-discovery-myths-causality|Mirror Neurons: Discovery, Myths, Causality Debates]] — original discovery and properties; intentionality encoding; what mirror neurons cannot explain (felt empathy); causality debates with Hickok | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/theory-of-mind-mirror-neurons-status-hierarchies|Theory of Mind, Mirror Neurons, and Status Hierarchies]] — mentalizing via vmPFC/TPJ; integration of perspective-taking with social rank; serotonin-mediated status effects on cognition | status: developing | sources: 1

---

## INTERMEDIATE LEVEL — Motivation, Reward, and Stress

*The dopamine system of pursuit, the cortisol system of threat, and how they shape behavior*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/dopamine-systems-and-motivation|Dopamine Systems and Motivation: The Engine of Pursuit, Not Pleasure]] — mesolimbic vs. mesocortical pathways; prediction error signal; uncertainty and "the maybe effect"; addiction architecture; temporal discounting; why dopamine ≠ pleasure but motivation | status: stable | sources: 3 | density: HIGH
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/cortisol-hpa-axis-stress-cascade|Cortisol & HPA Axis: The Allostatic Ratchet]] — HPA axis mechanism; acute vs. chronic stress; amygdala hyperexcitability; prefrontal degradation; stress-induced empathy collapse; structural brain changes from sustained cortisol elevation | status: stable | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/glucocorticoids-and-stress-response|Glucocorticoids and Stress Response]] — acute vs chronic cortisol effects; hippocampal atrophy; dendritic retraction; ACC-suppression mechanism | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/glucocorticoids-pain-matrix-stress-embodiment|Glucocorticoids, Pain Matrix, and Stress Embodiment]] — how stress hormones modulate insula and ACC pain-observation responses; the embodiment of chronic stress | status: developing | sources: 1

# Gigerenzer's Depth Psychology & The Soul's History — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers

Wolfgang Gigerenzer's systematic interrogation of how consciousness becomes psychological consciousness, grounded in a radical critique of contemporary psychology's defensive evasion of soul-encounter. This 31-page hub maps Gigerenzer's thesis: the soul requires sacrifice—destructive force, rupture, death, negation—as intrinsic to its self-realization. Archaic sacrificial practices represent the soul's most authentic expression before this violence became symbolized and unconsciously repressed in modernity.

The hub moves from: methodological foundations (what makes psychology possible) → historical pivot (where Western consciousness irreversibly diverged) → psychological foundations (the conditions that created the discipline) → consciousness development framework (how consciousness encounters otherness) → psychological development (shadow, anima, animus, sacrifice) → modernity's crisis (therapeutic evasion, Platonism, emancipation from sacrifice) → reference and applications.

**Core insight**: Contemporary psychology has become anti-psychological—it inverts the soul's actual operations to protect ego-consciousness from contact with necessity. Real psychology requires: abandonment of hope, acceptance of violence as necessity, and reckoning with archaic consciousness modernity repressed.

---

## How to Navigate This Hub

This hub is organized in layers, each building systematic understanding:

- **FOUNDATIONAL METHODOLOGY** — The philosophical/methodological architecture that enables psychology
- **HISTORICAL WATERSHED** — Where consciousness changed structure irreversibly
- **PSYCHOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS** — Why psychology emerged and what it requires
- **CONSCIOUSNESS DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK** — How consciousness encounters otherness through systematic stances
- **PSYCHOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT PROPER** — Shadow, anima, animus, sacrifice across history
- **MODERNITY'S CRISIS & RESPONSE** — Why contemporary psychology fails; what modernity lost
- **REFERENCE & HISTORICAL CONTEXT** — Biographical, anthropological, and application materials

## Key Tensions in This Hub

- **Soul in depths vs. soul in manifestation**: Does the soul exist in the imaginal/symbolic realm (Hillman) or in concrete historical manifestation (Gigerenzer)? Both are true, but one has psychological consequence: depth without manifestation is evasion.

- **Therapeutic helping vs. psychological encounter**: Are these compatible (contemporary psychology assumes) or fundamentally incompatible (Gigerenzer insists)? The conflict reveals psychology's defensive posture.

- **Archaic consciousness as wisdom vs. archaic consciousness as repressed**: Was the archaic civilization more conscious (and modernity regressed) or did consciousness develop in modernity (while repressing its foundation)? # Identity Architecture and Defense — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers

This hub maps the territory of identity construction as a defensive system. The core insight: identity is not "who you are" but rather a protective structure built to manage unbearable relational conditions. What feels like "your personality" is actually a concealment strategy — a way of organizing yourself to survive in an environment where certain aspects of yourself would be dangerous if revealed.

The pages here treat identity not as static essence but as functional defense. This reframe produces a radically different understanding of personal change: you cannot change identity through willpower or insight because identity is primarily a nervous system adaptation, not a belief. And you cannot abandon identity without grieving the loss of the defensive structure it has provided, understanding what made the defense necessary in the first place, and building a new relational context where the defense is no longer required.

## BEGINNER LEVEL — Hughes Six-Minute X-Ray: Defensive-Identity Reading Apparatus

*Chase Hughes — *Six-Minute X-Ray* (2020). Five 6MX pages housed here because they comprise the operator-side reading apparatus for *defensive identity structures* — the nonverbal, verbal, and integrative tools that read identity's protective architecture as it's expressed in conversation. Where the rest of this hub describes identity defense from inside (what the defense feels like, why it formed, how to work with it therapeutically), the Hughes pages describe it from outside (what the defense looks like to a trained observer, how to read it in real-time). The two perspectives are complementary diagnostic frameworks for the same psychological architecture. Companion pages housed primarily in [[ARCHIVES/concepts/hubs/manipulation-and-influence-hub|Manipulation and Influence Hub]]. Source: [[ARCHIVES/sources/hughes-six-minute-x-ray|Hughes — Six-Minute X-Ray (2020)]]. Tag: `[POPULAR SOURCE]`.*

## Key Tensions in This Area

**Identity as essence vs. identity as defense:** Is your personality who you "are," or is it a protective structure your nervous system built to manage relational threat? This determines whether change means "becoming someone else" (terrifying) or "stopping a protection that's no longer necessary" (possible).

**Shame as problem vs. shame as signal:** Is shame the enemy to be eliminated, or the nervous system's accurate signal that you're operating outside the relational boundaries you learned in your family of origin? The answer determines whether healing means "feeling less shame" or "updating what activates shame."

**Integration vs. acceptance:** Can the disowned material be genuinely integrated into a coherent self, or is the best outcome learning to operate from both primary and disowned selves with awareness of their separate operation?

## Structural Notes

**Hub construction note:** This hub integrates 15 existing psychology pages with 3 new synthetic bridge pages (reference-dependence, mental-accounting, sunk-costs) that apply behavioral economics mechanisms to identity architecture. The bridge pages are the conceptual integration point: they explain *why* identities are so persistent (loss aversion, sunk cost), *how* they're maintained despite contradicting evidence (mental accounting, reference dependence), and *what* makes them feel like literal self rather than protective structure (reference point anchoring).

The 8 concealment archetypes are the practical expression of these mechanisms at different reference points. Each archetype answers a different approval source and organizes around a different shame trigger. Understanding the economic principles (sunk cost, loss aversion, mental accounting) explains why intellectual understanding of the archetype doesn't produce change.

## Footnotes and Sources

Identity architecture drawing on: shame theory (Brown, Tangney), defense mechanisms (Cramer, Vaillant), concealment work (Heath, Teerikangas), relational development (Ainsworth, Howe), character structure (Chödrön, Gurdjieff), and behavioral economics applied to psychology (Kahneman & Tversky, Ariely). The vault synthesis treats identity as primarily a nervous system adaptation organized by relational threat rather than a cognitive or emotional construction.

# Inner Child & Child Psychology — Map of Content

## What This Hub Covers

This hub maps the psychology of the inner child — the authentic self that existed before wounding, the wounds that distorted or buried it, and the clinical and transpersonal work required to recover it. Pages span Bradshaw's shame framework, Whitfield's Child Within model, Kalsched's depth-psychological account of trauma's inner guardians, Janov's primal pain theory, Stone's sub-personality approach, and Grof's transpersonal extension of the recovery arc. Together they form the most comprehensive cluster in the psychology domain — 65 pages covering everything from the original wound to the spiritual state available on the other side of it.

---

## BEGINNER LEVEL — What the Inner Child Is: The Core Concept

*Start here. These five pages define the territory and establish the foundational claims the rest of the hub builds on.*

- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/real-self-vs-co-dependent-self|Real Self vs. Co-dependent Self]] — Whitfield: the buried authentic child versus the protective false persona that replaced it and how to tell them apart | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/vulnerable-child-inner-child|Vulnerable Child & Inner Child]] — Stone's sub-personality account of the child self hiding under the inner critic's armor; what happens when it never gets protection | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/the-child-archetype-in-world-mythology|The Child Archetype in World Mythology]] — Jung and Kalsched: the divine child as a universal image of renewal; why this archetype appears everywhere and what it reveals about psychic structure | status: developing | sources: 1
- [[ARCHIVES/concepts/psychology/innocence-and-its-loss|Innocence and Its Loss]] — Kalsched's account of what trauma takes when it shatters the child's original trust; the structure of the pre-traumatic self | status: developing | sources: 1
